conditions: Commutative ringed-space base, locally split extensions 0→Li→Ei→Mi→0; the concrete counterexample uses locally free O_X-extensions.
Interpret the frozen uncertain final splitting relation as psi_i varpi_i = chi id_Mi, and retain alpha_i pi_i + varpi_i psi_i = chi id_Ei and pi_i alpha_i = chi id_Li.
Use the standard pushout quotient (B⊕N)/{(mu(s),−pi(s))}, positive inclusion of N=L1⊗L2, and the standard pullback with the same positive kernel identification.

independent_derivation.pullback_conditions: In tensor coordinates, the pullback lift above m has (b,c,d)=(-tau1*m,-tau2*m,chi*m), and free kernel coordinate a.
independent_derivation.candidate_comparison: k=delta*tau1⊗tau2 changes by delta*chi*t, so the gluing defect is (delta*chi−2)t.
independent_derivation.sign_twist: F(n)=−n on the subobject and F(v)=w on local splittings is compatible with v′−v=t and w′−w=−t, so negating the subobject removes this obstruction.

counterexample.base: Smooth elliptic curve X over a characteristic-zero field
counterexample.global_maps: pi_i=psi_i and varpi_i=−alpha_i; all three splitting relations hold globally.
counterexample.local_tau: tau_i=1 for every local splitting s_i, because psi_i s_i=id.
counterexample.extension_classes: Take first input class e≠0 in H1(X,O_X), second class 0. Pushout class is e, pullback class is −e with fixed endpoint identifications.
counterexample.obstruction: 2e≠0 in characteristic zero, so no extension morphism inducing identities on both ends exists; such a morphism would be an isomorphism.
counterexample.hypotheses_satisfied: The quotient O_X is locally free, hence the extensions are locally split and their inclusions universally injective.

outcome: CONFIRMED: E170.4 and E170.5 have the correct signs and qualifications under their explicitly stated conventions.
